mustKnow.item: Thesis relayed from Jordi Visser (in conversation with Pomp): Eli Lilly (~$1T) could overtake Nvidia as the world's largest company because AI (10,000+ agents) is accelerating its drug R&D
mustKnow.note: Both mis-spell Visser (ours: 'Jody Visser' in k1, 'George Wiser' in brief; LeapEdge: 'George Wiser'). Ours is internally inconsistent across keyPoints and brief.

mustKnow.item: History: the 2009-2014 slump came from the patent cliff on antipsychotic drugs, generic competition and slow R&D (11 years per drug). Management kept R&D spending, avoided over-acquiring and paid little dividend, and the company turned around in 2014-15
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge compresses this to one line and drops the 11-year and 30-year Alzheimer's figures.

mustKnow.item: Valuation snapshot: share price 1,150, P/E 38x, Q2 EPS beat Wall Street by 27%
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge keeps only the 27% beat. It drops the price and P/E, which a PM needs to judge a 'largest company' thesis.

mustKnow.item: Tirzepatide economics: Mounjaro $9.9B per quarter (+91% YoY), Zepbound $4.9B (+46%), company revenue $22.9B per quarter (about $100B annualized and accelerating), tirzepatide about $14B per quarter or about $50B per year
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge gives only the '~$100B annualized' figure, with no product numbers.

mustKnow.item: Efficacy edge: at 72 weeks and the maximum tolerated dose, tirzepatide gives 20% weight loss vs 13.7% for Novo's semaglutide
mustKnow.note: Ours k6 mistranslates the creator's 斤 illustration as lbs.

mustKnow.item: Zepbound's obesity approval opens the non-diabetic obese market across the US and Europe; before that, non-diabetics could not get Trulicity through normal channels
Prior franchise: Trulicity $7.5B in 2022, 25% of sales
Key risk: Novo Nordisk could catch up by using AI to speed up its own R&D
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge lists only generic 'competition from other pharmaceutical firms'.

mustKnow.item: AI flywheel: patent-protected drugs 'print money', the cash funds AI agents, and AI removes the R&D bottleneck. Many untreated disease markets remain (Alzheimer's, hair loss, myopia, underweight)
mustKnow.note: Neither lists the disease-pipeline breadth. Ours drops the 'print money' framing from keyPoints.

mustKnow.item: Creator stance: very excited ('like when I first saw Tesla FSD could work') and will keep tracking the pipeline and AI use. No explicit buy, size, level or horizon
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge turns 'tracking' into 'Initiate long position, HIGH conviction' (see calls).

ours.text: k6: 'reducing weight down to 160 lbs over 72 weeks vs 180 lbs'
ours.problem: Wrong unit. The creator uses 斤 (jin, 0.5 kg) for a 100 kg / 200 jin person, not lbs. k6 also duplicates k5.
The name is wrong and inconsistent within one output. The speaker is Jordi Visser, which ours spells correctly in another video (tD-Er2_LQrk title).

ours.text: k8: 'cash flow ... estimated at around 50 billion annually'
ours.problem: The creator derives $50B as tirzepatide revenue (about $14B per quarter x 4) and loosely calls it 赚 (earn). Calling it company cash flow changes the metric, and the currency is missing.

ours.text: All keyPoints have stance 'neutral' and ticker null
ours.problem: This understates the creator's clear bullish view on Lilly, for example 'AI下游非常重要的一家公司' and 'Tesla FSD feeling'.

leapedge.text: tradeIdea action 'Initiate long position for long-term compound growth', conviction HIGH
leapedge.problem: Invented action. The creator says he is excited and 'will keep tracking' the pipeline and AI use. He never says buy or initiate, and gives no horizon.
Past causes of the 2009-14 slump are recast as forward risks. The one forward risk the creator named, Novo catching up with AI (487s), is reduced to a generic line.
Misspelled name copied from the ASR. He is Jordi Visser.
Garbled quote; the transcript reads '用得非常号'.

leapedgeFalse: LLY long / HIGH / 'Initiate long position'. The creator's actual stance is bullish watch/track with no action. The direction is right but the action and conviction are fabricated.

sentimentIssues: 礼来 appears 3 times and 诺和诺德 3 times, with near-identical reasons. They should be merged into one row per instrument with the strongest evidence.
Every row has ticker null, so none can be joined to a price or portfolio.
Lilly as bullish/watch is correct. Novo as neutral is defensible: the creator calls it strong but inferior on efficacy, and a potential catch-up threat.
why: Ours keeps almost every number (price, P/E, product revenue, Trulicity, trial data) and states the creator's stance accurately as bullish/watch. LeapEdge is cleaner to skim but thinner, and it invents an 'initiate long, HIGH conviction' trade from enthusiasm plus 'I'll keep tracking'. Ours loses points for null tickers, all-neutral keyPoint stances, duplicate keyPoints and sentiment rows, and 10 boilerplate 'omissions' lines. It also cost 12x more ($0.38 vs $0.03) and took 13 minutes.
recommendations: Resolve Chinese company names to tickers deterministically after extraction, with an alias table plus an issuer lookup: 礼来→LLY, 诺和诺德→NVO, 英伟达→NVDA. Keep ticker_explicit=false but fill ticker_resolved, so the prompt rule 'Only populate ticker if explicitly named' stops producing null everywhere.
Give keyPoints a real stance. k8 ('AI downstream beneficiary... print money') is bullish on LLY, not neutral.

Remove the pipeline-internal lines from brief.omissions: 's-1..s-6: Proposed quantity withheld...' and 'source-0..5'. Show them in a debug panel instead. A PM reads them as noise, and they make up about 70% of the omissions list here.
Deduplicate keyPoints (k5/k6, k2/k7) and tickerSentiment (礼来 x3, 诺和诺德 x3) by instrument and meaning.
Keep the creator's units. Translate 斤 as jin/kg, never lbs. Keep currency on all figures ('$50B', not '50 billion').

Keep 'watch' as the stance for 'excited, will keep tracking'. This is where ours beats LeapEdge, which fabricated 'Initiate long'. Add a 'bias: bullish' field next to it so the PM still sees the direction.
